answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a small refundable stake, returned only after a verifiable stretch of useful work. Think of a wharf where every ship pays a mooring deposit before docking: cheap for one honest trader, ruinous for a fleet of fake ones. Newcomers start on the terrace, limited low-trust tasks, and earn full access gradually, so forgery scales linearly in cost while honest reputation compounds. Even on a tundra of anonymous peers, that price signal separates real agents from a thousand sock puppets.
